question: What is the primary reason single-drug therapy is never used to treat active tuberculosis?

options.A: It is completely inactivated by gastric acid in the stomach
options.B: It causes rapid destruction of normal gut flora
options.C: It leads to the rapid emergence of drug-resistant bacterial strains
options.D: It fails to cross the thick waxy cell wall of the bacillus

explanation: Spontaneous mutations causing drug resistance occur naturally, so using only one drug allows resistant mutants to survive and multiply unchecked. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why must tuberculosis treatment be carried out over several months rather than a standard one-week course?

options.A: First-line medications accumulate slowly in human tissues and take months to reach therapeutic thresholds
options.B: The drugs take at least three months just to absorb into systemic circulation
options.C: Patients require long periods of hospital isolation to prevent airborne spread
options.D: Tubercle bacilli have very slow replication rates and can remain dormant inside granulomas

explanation: Slow-growing and dormant persister cells require prolonged exposure to combination chemotherapy to be fully eradicated and prevent relapse. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which first-line anti-tuberculosis drug is known for imparting a reddish-orange color to urine, tears, and sweat?
explanation: Rifampicin is a colored compound that safely discolors body fluids, a harmless effect that must be explained to patients to prevent panic. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which Isoniazid exerts its bactericidal effect on Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

options.A: Inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis at the 30S ribosomal subunit
options.C: Disrupting the synthesis of mycolic acid in the bacterial cell wall
options.D: Chelating essential divalent cations in the bacterial cytoplasm

explanation: Isoniazid targets the pathways responsible for building mycolic acid, compromising the integrity of the mycobacterial cell wall. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is a major characteristic of second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs compared to first-line agents?

options.A: They generally possess lower potency and higher toxicity profiles
options.B: They are significantly cheaper and more widely available
options.C: They never require laboratory susceptibility testing before use
options.D: They can be administered safely for only three days total

explanation: Second-line agents are reserved for resistant cases because they are harder to tolerate and less efficient at clearing bacilli than standard first-line drugs. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h3)

question: A patient with multi-drug resistant tuberculosis is prescribed a fluoroquinolone such as moxifloxacin. What is the cellular target of this drug class?

options.A: Bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
options.B: Arabinosyl transferase enzymes in the cell wall

explanation: Fluoroquinolones disrupt bacterial DNA replication by inhibiting vital enzymes responsible for DNA supercoiling. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the standard duration for the intensive phase of treatment in a newly diagnosed, drug-susceptible tuberculosis case?
explanation: The intensive phase utilizes all four first-line drugs daily for the first two months to achieve rapid reduction of the bacterial burden. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: A public health nurse is setting up a community program to improve treatment completion rates for local tuberculosis patients. Which intervention best describes the core concept of DOTS?

options.A: Having a trained healthcare worker observe the patient swallow every prescribed dose
options.B: Requiring monthly sputum microscopy tests before releasing the next drug refill
options.C: Providing financial incentives once the entire six-month course of medications is finished
options.D: Mailing monthly supplies of anti-tuberculosis pills directly to the patient's home address

explanation: Directly Observed Therapy requires physical observation of medication ingestion to guarantee adherence and prevent drug resistance. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which anti-tuberculosis medication is most commonly associated with causing peripheral neuropathy, which can be prevented by co-administering Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
explanation: Isoniazid increases excretion and inhibits activation of pyridoxine, precipitating peripheral nerve damage unless vitamin supplementation is given. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: A patient taking Ethambutol reports difficulty distinguishing between red and green traffic lights and blurred vision. What is the nurse's best interpretation of these symptoms?

options.A: Early warning signs of Ethambutol-induced optic neuritis requiring immediate medical review
options.B: Normal neurological adaptation to intensive phase tuberculosis drugs
options.C: Peripheral neuropathy caused by a lack of dietary Vitamin B6 intake
options.D: A harmless side effect of rifampicin interacting with dietary pigments

explanation: Ethambutol toxicity can damage the optic nerve, altering color vision and acuity; prompt discontinuation or dose adjustment usually prevents permanent blindness. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h5)

question: A patient who has been on tuberculosis treatment for four weeks states they want to stop taking their pills because their cough has completely gone away. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Advise the patient to double their daily dose so they can finish the remaining supply in half the scheduled time
options.B: Agree with the patient since symptom resolution indicates total elimination of all bacteria
options.C: Explain that feeling better means the active bacteria are suppressed, but full treatment duration is necessary to kill dormant germs and prevent a drug-resistant relapse
options.D: Tell the patient to switch to herbal remedies since the pharmaceutical drugs have already done their job

explanation: Symptom disappearance occurs long before sterilizing eradication of dormant bacilli; finishing the full course is vital to prevent relapse. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary nursing responsibility during the management of a patient receiving anti-tuberculosis medications?

options.A: Monitoring liver function tests and watching for signs of jaundice
options.B: Providing strict instructions on dietary sodium restriction
options.C: Assessing for visual changes and peripheral neuropathy
options.D: Ensuring direct observation of medication swallowing

explanation: Standard tuberculosis regimens do not require sodium restriction; monitoring liver function, neurotoxicity, and ensuring adherence are the core duties. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h6)
